title: Counting, Corners, Leading & Look-Ahead
description: Native staggering from sibling-index(), superellipse corners, trimmed half-leading, predicted pointer events, and self-sizing fields.

drops.title: Stagger Without Counting
drops.description: sibling-index() and sibling-count() hand CSS an element's own position, so a stagger re-times itself when the list changes.
drops.concept: Staggered motion has always meant a ladder of :nth-child() rules or a JS loop writing --i onto every node, and both break the moment the list is edited. These two functions return position and group size as plain integers usable inside calc(), so animation-delay: calc(sibling-index() * 60ms) is the whole mechanism. The drop adds, removes and shuffles rows live to show the delays re-deriving themselves; where the functions are missing a six-line shim writes the same custom properties.
drops.source: Frontend Masters blog — Staggered Animation with CSS sibling-* Functions

interaction.mouse: Sliders retime the stagger step, duration and travel distance live
interaction.click: Add, remove and shuffle list rows; reverse the grid order via sibling-count(); replay
interaction.touch: All controls are tap targets; the grid and equaliser animate unprompted

drops.title: The Corner Is a Curve Now
drops.description: corner-shape separates a corner's size from its geometry — one exponent slides from a scoop through a circle to a squircle.
drops.concept: border-radius has only ever controlled how big a corner is, which is why every squircle on the web was an SVG clip-path or a bitmap. corner-shape draws the curve inside the corner box the radius defines, and superellipse(k) makes it a continuous dial: -1 scoops inward, 0 bevels, 1 is the familiar arc, 2 is the iOS squircle, and large k approaches a hard square. Corners are addressable individually, and the whole thing degrades to plain rounded corners where it is unsupported.
drops.source: Squircle.js blog — Squircles in CSS: corner-shape, superellipse() and browser support

interaction.mouse: Drag the exponent and radius sliders to reshape every corner on the page at once
interaction.click: Keyword presets — scoop, bevel, round, squircle, square; bento tiles lift on hover
interaction.touch: Sliders and preset pills are touch-sized; tiles respond to tap

drops.title: Cutting the Invisible Leading
drops.description: text-box-trim removes the half-leading a font reserves above its caps and below its baseline, so padding means what it says.
drops.concept: Every font reserves vertical space around its letters, which is why a heading never optically sits where its box claims and why designers have shipped a decade of magic negative margins. text-box-trim cuts that space off the first and last line box; text-box-edge chooses the landmark to cut back to — cap height, x-height, or the font's own declared text edges. The drop overlays the actual line box so you can measure the difference, then shows it paying off in a stat tile, a button and a pill.
drops.source: Piccalilli — Why I'm excited about text-box-trim as a designer

interaction.mouse: Dropdowns switch trim mode and edge landmark; a slider drives line-height
interaction.click: Toggle the tinted overlay that reveals the real text box
interaction.touch: Selects and slider work as native touch controls

drops.title: Ahead of the Finger
drops.description: getPredictedEvents() hands you the browser's guess at where the pointer is going, so a drag renders ahead of the input instead of behind it.
drops.concept: A drag is always late: by the time a pointermove is handled, laid out and composited, the finger has moved on, and that gap is what 'laggy' feels like. getPredictedEvents() returns the browser's own extrapolation of the pointer's path from recent velocity and trajectory, so you can render at the predicted position and let reality catch up. The drop races three followers against one pointer — the raw stream, the pointermove position and the predicted one — and measures in pixels how much of the lag prediction actually recovers.

interaction.mouse: Drag across the field — fast curving strokes open the biggest gap between the three followers
interaction.click: Toggle prediction off to watch the gold puck fall back onto the grey one; sliders set look-ahead, simulated frame cost and trail length
interaction.touch: Touch drags drive the same three followers; the panel sits inline above the demos on a phone

drops.title: Fields That Fit Their Contents
drops.description: field-sizing: content deletes the auto-growing textarea script — fields size themselves and max-width still bounds them.
drops.concept: The auto-growing textarea is the most re-implemented component on the web, and every version has the same three bugs: it lags a keystroke behind, it forgets to shrink, and it fights the scrollbar at the boundary. field-sizing: content hands the job to the layout engine, which already knew how tall the text was. A textarea grows and shrinks, an input hugs its value, a select resizes to the chosen option — with ordinary max-height and max-width doing the bounding.
drops.source: Wes Bos — Auto growing textarea with CSS field-sizing: content

interaction.mouse: Type in the composer and watch it grow, then stop at max-height and scroll
interaction.click: Paste a paragraph, add and remove tags, compare the two sizing modes side by side
interaction.touch: All fields are native inputs; the bound sliders work under touch
